newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electric test car catches fire in Sweden, 15 hurt.
newsitem.headline: Electric test car catches fire in Sweden, 15 hurt.

text.p: Fifteen people were treated in hospital for smoke inhalation after a new type of battery in an electric test car caught fire in Stockholm on Thursday.
Clouds of potassium hydroxide gas billowed out from the car's batteries, said a spokeswoman for the Swedish state-owned utility group Vattenfall, the firm testing the vehicle.
Firemen had trouble putting out the blaze and at least 15 people required hospital treatment. All but two had been discharged by early evening.

Vattenfall is testing two of the vehicles in a year-long project with the Swedish post office. Sixty more of the cars, developed by Electric Fuel Limited of Israel, are being tested by Germany's post office Deutsche Bundespost, the spokeswoman said.
Swedish news agency TT quoted Vattenfall project leader Leif Brandells as saying the cause of the fire was unknown.
"The advantage of this particular battery is that the car can go 300-400 km (190-250 miles) on one charge instead of the normal 60 km (37 miles)," Brandells said.
